title: Urban sprawl and urban consolidation
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:16Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-20T12:25:47Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point, geo-suburbanisation-urban-sprawl, covers only sprawl at Year 12 depth and does not teach urban consolidation, which the new point needs, so adding it would be a new idea rather than a small change.

draft.title: Urban sprawl and urban consolidation
card: the spread of a city outward onto land at its edge, such as farmland and bushland. New houses and roads are built where there were few before.
fitting more homes into suburbs that already exist. Examples are apartments, units and townhouses built near train stations and shops.
Sprawl can take farmland and bush, and it can mean longer trips to work and school. Consolidation can use roads, trains and services that are already built.
Consolidation can bring problems too. Existing suburbs may become more crowded, with more traffic and pressure on local services.
draft.remember: Sprawl grows the city outward. Consolidation fits more homes inside it.

a.q: Which change in a city is an example of urban consolidation?
opts: Apartments replace old houses beside a train station
New estates are built on farmland at the city edge
A new road opens up bushland for more housing
A town on the city fringe is joined to the city by homes
a.why: Apartments beside a train station add homes inside an existing suburb, which is consolidation. The other options all spread housing outward onto new land, which is sprawl.
a.clue: Look for the option that adds homes without using new land.

b.q: A council in outer Sydney approves 2000 new houses on former farmland. Which describes this and one likely effect?
opts: Urban sprawl, which can mean longer trips to work
Urban sprawl, which can use existing trains and shops
Urban consolidation, which can mean longer trips to work
Urban consolidation, which can use existing trains and shops
b.why: Building houses on former farmland at the city edge is urban sprawl. Homes far from the centre can mean longer trips to work. Using existing trains and shops is a possible benefit of consolidation, not sprawl.
b.clue: Ask where the new homes are built: inside the city or at its edge.

a.best: Apartments replace old houses beside a train station

b.best: Urban sprawl, which can mean longer trips to work
